DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, February 27, 1924.

DEAR SIR, - I beg to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of the 25th instant, with reference to payments made by
this Department to Mr. Myles Morley as Inspector of Construction at the Fraser Lake Indian boarding school since
July, 1922. I have noted what you say, that is, that when an Inspector of Construction is employed continuously during
the month his services should be paid at the monthly rate.

In reply I beg to say that the certificates of temporary appointment were issued by the Civil Service Commission for
certain specified periods with remuneration at the rate of $6 per day. No mention was made of a monthly rate, and the
Department paid at the rate which was provided for in the certificates. However, in the future we will be guided by
your interpretation of the regulations, and, in employing men as Inspectors of Construction, we will specify that they
are to be paid at the rate of $6 per day, but that their monthly remuneration must not exceed $140, the maximum
provided under the classification schedule.

The last paragraph of your letter has been noted.


Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Assistant Auditor General.

Vote 279, Indian Education: Payments to Wyatt-Ireland, Limited, for repairs to Elkhorn Indian School


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, May 23, 1924.



=== EXTRACT FROM HERE (pages 565-568) ===
<!-- page 565 -->
SIR, - Messrs. Wyatt-Ireland Limited of Winnipeg were paid the amount of $80,360.36 during the fiscal year 1923 -
24 for repairs, and alterations to the Elkhorn Indian School. According to the accounts received at this office the
payments were made on a basis of actual cost plus ten per centum.

<!-- page 566 -->
On inquiry being made at your accountant's branch, this office was given to understand that no formal contract had
been entered into with Wyatt-Ireland Limited for the execution of the work. A notation on the statements of account,
however, appears to indicate the work was proceeded with under the authority of departmental letter No. 106-0-5D of
July 20th, 1923; I have to ask that you will kindly supply me with a copy of that letter.

Section 36 of the Public Works Act enacts that "Whenever any works are to be executed under the direction of any
department of the Government, the Minister having charge of such department shall invite tenders by public
advertisement for the execution of such works, except in cases - (a) of pressing emergency in which delay would be
injurious to the public interest; or (b) in which from the nature of the work it can be more expeditiously and
economically executed by the officers and servants of the department; or (c) where the estimated cost of the work is
less than five thousand dollars and it appears to the Minister, in view of the nature of the work, that it is not advisable
to invite tenders."

Subsection 2 of the same section requires that when tenders are invited all tenders received shall be submitted to and
the contract awarded under the direction of the Governor in Council.

As public tenders do not appear to have been invited in this case, I have to request you to inform me under which
clause of the section quoted above this work was undertaken without calling for tenders.


I am, Sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, July 7, 1924.

DEAR SIR, - I have to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of May 23rd, with reference to the expenditure for
repairs and alterations to the Elkhorn industrial school.

This work was carried out by authority of the Minister under Section 36, subsection "A" of the Public Works Act as it
was work of pressing emergency. The Department had for some time been considering re-opening the school under
Church of England auspices, and when it was finally decided to do so, it was advisable that the work of renovating the
school should be done immediately. The alterations and repairs were under the supervision of an officer of the Public
Works Department who certified all accounts. The building had fallen into a state of dilapidation as it had been to all
intents unoccupied for five years.

As requested I am enclosing herewith a copy of letter of the 20th July, 1923.


Yours truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Assistant Auditor General.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, July 20, 1923.

DEAR SIR, - With reference to the repairs required to the heating, plumbing, sewage disposal system and the building
at the Elkhorn Industrial School, I am enclosing herewith copy of a report received from Mr. R. Thomson, Mechanical
Engineer of Department of Public Works, Winnipeg, outlining the work required to put the mechanical equipment and
the building in good condition.

<!-- page 567 -->

<!-- page 568 -->
You are authorized to have the work as recommended by Mr. Thomson carried out, and to employ the contracting firm
of Wyatt & Ireland 505 Lombard Building, Winnipeg, to undertake the work. They will be paid on a proven cost plus
ten per cent basis. It will therefore be necessary that detailed accounts be kept by them and furnished you of all labour
and materials required in the work. These should be carefully checked and forwarded to the Department.

Mr. Thomson has intimated that he is willing to furnish detailed instructions to the contractors with reference to this
work, and I would ask you to please consult with him in the matter. The Department would be very pleased if he would
render whatever services are required to expedite the work. I would also ask you to keeps the Department posted from
time to time as to the progress being made in the work.

As requested, I am returning herewith the blue print copy of the septic tank which you forwarded to the Department
and asked to have returned.

If the building is to be ready for occupation this fall, it will be necessary that the work as outlined in Mr. Thomson's
report be carried out with all possible despatch.


Your obedient servant,
A.F. MACKENZIE, Act. Asst. Deputy.


JOHN R. BUNN, Inspector of Indian Agencies, Winnipeg, Man.

Vote 279, Indian Education: Grant towards erection of Wing at St. Bruno's Indian School


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, June 16, 1924.

SIR, - Cheque No. 6370 issued in March last and charged against the vote for Indian Education is for the payment of
$10,775.85 to Rev. C. Falher, O.M.I., as a grant towards the erection of a wing at St. Bruno's Indian Residential School
which was destroyed by fire during the winter of 1923 - 24.

According to the vouchers submitted in support of this payment, your department, with the approval of the
Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, offered the Bishop of Athabasca a grant of $12,000 towards the rebuilding.
The church authorities were to be responsible for the labour on the building and were to present receipted accounts for
the material purchased and for the freighting. The payment in question represents the receipted accounts that have been
presented, but a number of the receipted accounts attached to the vouchers indicate the total amount paid, without
giving any particulars as to the quantity and prices of the materials furnished.

I am of opinion that the authority of the Governor in Council should have been obtained before an expenditure of this
nature was incurred.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, June 24, 1924.
